newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Bankar-B in pact with Gog Securities.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Bankar-B in pact with Gog Securities.

text.p: Hungary's Bankar-B Rt, member of the Bankar financial group, said on Thursday it was joining forces with Budapest Stock Exchange member Gog Securities but that they did not plan to merge.

"We are talking about long-term cooperation, about the fusion of activities, but not about one company swallowing the other," Bankar-B's chairman and general director Imre Rethy told a news conference.

The deal is in line with Bankar's plan to move towards retail clients, as so far it has focused on institutional clients. The move will also help in its wish to acquire membership of the stock exchange, Rethy said.
The cooperation also fits in with the plans of Gog Securities, one of the few privately held brokerages in Hungary, which stem from Hungary's new Securities Act which came into effect on January 1.

Under the Act the registered capital of an investment firm may be no less than 20 million forints for commission brokerage companies, one hundred million forints for securities trading companies and one billion forints for investment houses.

"The new Securities Act and the whole legal ruling... does not really favour private companies, therefore I decided half a year ago to find a partner on the Hungarian market who thinks in a similar way," said Gog's president and CEO Gabor Gog.
Most of Hungary's securities houses belong either to major foreign houses or are the investment arms of domestic banks.
Under the deal, Bankar will take over Gog's retail clientele of around 3,000 people and will buy Gog's Imperial Fund Management which handles two funds with 1.5 billion forints of assets.
Bankar-B will also take over more than 70 percent of Gog Securities' staff and will appoint Gabor Gog as Deputy General Director.
Bankar-B called an extraordinary general meeting for August 12 to raise its one billion forints capital by 90 million privately and to approve Gog as new board member, Rethy said.
